topics.title: Rental closing cost allocation
topics.trigger: A closing statement combines financing, acquisition and prepaid operating items.
topics.principle: Different closing entries can affect basis, financing costs or expenses differently. Preserve the transaction details instead of adding every line to the building cost.
topics.example: An investor pays loan fees, prepaid insurance and title charges at the same closing and imports the total into one asset account.

topics.title: Renovation contractor draw reconciliation
topics.trigger: A contractor bills progress draws rather than individual installed items.
topics.principle: A cash payment proves that money moved but may not identify completed work. Match draws, change orders and final invoices before creating an improvement record.
topics.example: An apartment owner pays three draws while electrical and plumbing work finish in different phases.

topics.title: Roof project repair review
topics.trigger: A roof project combines small repairs, replacement and related damage work.
topics.principle: Repair versus improvement analysis depends on the facts and applicable unit of property. A contractor's use of the word repair does not settle tax treatment.
topics.example: A landlord replaces one damaged section while the invoice also covers a larger roof upgrade and interior restoration.

topics.title: HVAC replacement documentation
topics.trigger: A rental replaces equipment that serves more than one unit or activity.
topics.principle: Identify the system, locations served and replaced components. The invoice needs enough detail to support capitalization, allocation and any disposition review.
topics.example: A mixed-use building installs new HVAC serving residential units and a ground-floor shop.

topics.title: Appliance replacement asset history
topics.trigger: A rental replaces refrigerators or other separately identified items.
topics.principle: Keep the purchase, location, readiness and old asset record connected. Do not count an item in both a new purchase schedule and an existing study cost pool.
topics.example: A landlord replaces appliances that were already separately tracked after an earlier cost segregation study.

topics.title: Furniture inventory at rental turnover
topics.trigger: Furniture changes as guests, owners and cleaners report loss or damage.
topics.principle: Use an inventory that distinguishes retained, replaced, sold and missing items. A listing photograph can corroborate an item but does not establish its acquisition cost.
topics.example: A furnished rental upgrades mattresses and sofas while the owner moves some old items into personal use.

topics.title: Security deposit accounting
topics.trigger: A landlord holds tenant deposits and sometimes applies them to damage or unpaid rent.
topics.principle: Separate refundable funds from amounts later retained or applied. The lease terms and actual disposition matter more than the bank account label.
topics.example: A landlord collects a deposit, returns most of it at move-out and keeps the remainder for an itemized damage charge.

topics.title: Property manager statement reconciliation
topics.trigger: A manager collects rent and pays expenses before transferring cash to the owner.
topics.principle: Reconcile gross rent, expenses, reserves and owner distributions. The owner's net deposit is not a complete rental activity ledger.
topics.example: A manager holds a maintenance reserve and deducts repairs while the owner records only monthly transfers.

topics.title: Rental insurance claim restoration
topics.trigger: Insurance proceeds and repair invoices arrive at different times after property damage.
topics.principle: Document the event, damaged assets, payments and restoration separately. A claim settlement does not by itself determine casualty, basis or repair treatment.
topics.example: A storm damages a duplex and the insurer pays an advance before the final restoration invoice is available.

topics.title: Rental property tax escrow reconciliation
topics.trigger: Mortgage payments include escrow deposits that differ from actual tax payments.
topics.principle: Keep lender escrow funding distinct from the taxing authority payment. Annual statements can explain why the cash flow and tax expense differ.
topics.example: An owner pays a higher monthly mortgage escrow amount after reassessment but the county tax payment occurs later.

topics.title: Rental placed-in-service evidence
topics.trigger: A rental is purchased, repaired, listed and first occupied on different dates.
topics.principle: Readiness and availability for the intended rental use need factual support. The purchase date and first booking are relevant evidence but are not interchangeable rules.
topics.example: An investor closes in August, completes required work in September and receives the first tenant payment in October.

topics.title: Rental conversion use records
topics.trigger: A property moves from personal use into a rental activity.
topics.principle: Conversion requires a supported use timeline and basis review. Original purchase price alone may not establish the appropriate depreciation starting point.
topics.example: An owner moves out of a home, makes improvements and begins offering it for rent several months later.

topics.title: Vacation rental owner stays
topics.trigger: Guests and the owner use the same property during the year.
topics.principle: Track actual days and purposes before applying rental, personal-use and expense allocation rules. A platform calendar does not resolve every blocked day.
topics.example: An owner blocks dates for family stays, maintenance trips and vacant days between guests.

topics.title: STR guest service evidence
topics.trigger: A short-term rental provides services that vary across bookings.
topics.principle: Document the actual operating services and frequency. Booking length alone does not settle reporting, activity classification or participation consequences.
topics.example: A property supplies periodic linen changes and optional daily cleaning while other bookings receive only turnover service.

topics.title: Rental participation task logs
topics.trigger: An owner wants a review of involvement in operating a rental.
topics.principle: Record tasks, dates and reasonable supporting evidence. Hours, managerial involvement, other participants and the applicable tests need analysis beyond a total on a spreadsheet.
topics.example: An owner coordinates repairs and guest issues while a manager handles most bookings and cleaning.

topics.title: Real estate professional work calendar
topics.trigger: A taxpayer performs work across rentals, a separate profession and other activities.
topics.principle: Real estate professional status and material participation are distinct analyses. Maintain complete facts rather than assuming ownership or a job title resolves either test.
topics.example: A medical professional reduces clinical days and begins personally managing several rentals during the year.

topics.title: Rental loan proceeds use tracing
topics.trigger: An owner refinances and distributes some proceeds while using other funds for improvements.
topics.principle: The use of borrowed funds is important to interest analysis. The property securing the loan does not by itself explain how every dollar was used.
topics.example: A rental refinance pays off an earlier loan, funds a renovation and transfers remaining cash to the owner's brokerage account.

topics.title: Rental sale asset register
topics.trigger: A rental sale includes land, building and separately tracked assets.
topics.principle: Retain the allocation, depreciation history and transaction facts. Sale proceeds and outstanding mortgage balance do not by themselves establish taxable gain.
topics.example: An investor sells a furnished rental after replacements and an earlier cost segregation study changed the asset schedule.

topics.title: Rental portfolio shared expenses
topics.trigger: An owner pays bills covering multiple properties and personal activity.
topics.principle: Document a reasonable, supportable allocation and preserve the source amount. A portfolio expense must not be recorded at full cost on every property.
topics.example: An owner receives one landscaping invoice covering three rentals and a personal residence.

topics.title: Prior rental depreciation gaps
topics.trigger: Old returns and available depreciation schedules do not agree.
topics.principle: Reconstruct the asset history before proposing a correction. The applicable procedure may depend on the nature and years of the error; do not assume every issue is resolved by an amended return.
topics.example: An investor supplies two returns but no asset schedule for a property first rented several years earlier.
